batch_strategy: Select interpretable condition-response and loading contrasts around demonstrated failures, then test transfer into related carbonyl, alcohol, ester, and nonpolar graphs. Give particular attention to scaffold-specific V2 growth and conflicting m202 observations. Include compact-response controls so corrections can generalize without spreading broad intervals across ordinary rows. Freeze these 32 IDs and their supplied premeasurement predictions before measurement.

choices.reason: m141 at 5/1, 150 uL fills the missing region between measured 1/1 record de4e10d3a5d448ffcdda and the broad 20/1 record 51f4126a3aadb3239225. Together with the selected 10/1 point, it locates where the methylpyridine finish begins its steep rise at fixed loading.

m141 at 10/1, 150 uL connects directly to measured 20/1 record 51f4126a3aadb3239225, whose historical V2 underprediction was about 47 mL. Comparison with measured 10/1, 50 uL record 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0 also tests whether loading changes onset and finish differently.

m37 at 20/1, 50 uL extends the fixed-loading curve through measured 5/1 record 4908bb1bf155952cd305 and 10/1 record 9ae9c8b491a04e429a11. It checks whether the broad finish measured at 20/1, 100 uL in b6f1b33a5491968c645e persists at lower loading, separating condition response from a local loading effect.

m31 at 5/1, 50 uL bridges measured 1/1 record 386303f0b10c49ce93b4 and the newly measured 10/1 record b3d9bb5afa82b99f2a11 at the same loading. This localizes the carbonyl-nitrile transition instead of learning its high-retention endpoint alone.

m209 at 5/1, 50 uL begins a matched intermediate curve between measured 2/1 record eda42a3c0f94ffce3e99 and 20/1 record 1b4be0410f927930d56e. The phenol may respond differently from the aromatic alcohol families; this is a testable chemical prior, not an established transition location.

m209 at 10/1, 50 uL pairs with its selected 5/1 point and measured 20/1 record 1b4be0410f927930d56e. The authoritative observed table contains no m209 10/1 measurement, so this supplies a genuinely missing point for learning the onset and finish response.

m36 at 1/1, 100 uL provides a fixed-loading comparison with measured 2/1 record 6b7209c2e8154837a8c7. With the low-ratio anchor 71d8b719ba209d117b05, it tests whether the amino-acetophenone response rises before 2/1 or mainly between 1/1 and 2/1.

m191 at 10/1, 100 uL extends the para-dialdehyde beyond measured 2/1 record acdffd73c7b1388ba321. Its large predictor quantile widths and high CW distance support testing whether two carbonyl groups produce a steep response like m31 or a different endpoint pattern.

m199 at 10/1, 150 uL tests the predicted leveling after the measured 5/1 intervals in 714004602e6452764d9a and f82cfd3b57735b0ead3c. It distinguishes a real sulfoxide plateau from insufficient condition sensitivity after the recent accurate 5/1 prediction.

m72 at 10/1, 150 uL with DCM loading fills the gap before repeated 20/1 measurements 334f7f55dcbf278e47ec and 5d6d4ac0c1dfacbde53d. It constrains where the genuinely broad amino-ester finish develops, rather than transferring its high-ratio width to the entire curve.

m72 at 10/1, 150 uL with PE loading pairs with the selected DCM-loading row. The loading-solvent volumes also differ, so this tests their joint recorded effect rather than isolating solvent identity. Measured PE records a047be17b8ee8bebb29a and 8e7636d7a60a6058305a anchor the lower and higher ratios.

m202 at 5/1, 50 uL pairs with the selected 100 uL row to test whether the striking mass contrast at 10/1 is already present at a lower ratio. Measured 7de812bda21b4dfe46dc and 902937db42f82f467718 differ substantially despite sharing the remaining recorded conditions.

m202 at 5/1, 100 uL tests the branch leading toward measured 10/1 record 902937db42f82f467718 at 35.08/70.35 mL. Its pairing with 50 uL is more discriminating than another isolated compact anchor, given the conflicting 150 uL result cb446680f62351d087a9.

m195 at 20/1, 50 uL adds a third loading level beside measured 100 uL record 783cf2454912fc14bb80 and 150 uL record a917c928912c74862968. The latter records V1 slightly above V2 and a much later onset. This label can constrain the loading surface while keeping record variability as an alternative explanation.

m19 at 2/1, 100 uL fills the midpoint between measured 50 and 150 uL records 6d21e9ec887b3408c612 and 906bd247e050658f99d8. Those labels show a roughly 10 mL onset shift with almost unchanged finish, making this a useful test of loading curvature despite modest current quantile widths.

m90 at 5/1, 100 uL creates a loading contrast with b51b5dbcd2a38b174973 and a condition contrast with 96710afeabc594baa359. Its 2/1 and 10/1 measured loading pairs show larger onset than finish movement; this tests whether that pattern transfers through the intermediate ratio.

Molecule-novel m179 at 10/1, 100 uL starts a matched two-condition experiment for the larger fused cyclic ketone. It tests transfer from the measured tetralone and methyl-tetralone families, including 983a604ac43bb4d41238 and 65f22906a14f74d756d4, without equating ring-size effects with a simple polarity correction.

Molecule-novel m179 at 50/1, 100 uL pairs with its 10/1 point at identical loading conditions. The pair separates a scaffold offset from solvent-response curvature and tests whether the predicted late finish transfers from related fused ketones.

Molecule-novel chalcone m165 at 50/1 tests transfer across conjugated carbonyl topology. Measured m164 records 5df546d9e2f2a29dfc89 and b7fffd840d208b29776c provide related conjugated-ketone anchors, but the extra aryl attachment and different conjugation pattern need not yield the same response.

m159 at 50/1 extends a nitrile-substituted diaryl ketone beyond compact measured 5/1 record b86ace0ccafe0af8ceec. It tests whether the strong response measured for acetyl nitrile m31 in b3d9bb5afa82b99f2a11 transfers to a diaryl carbonyl environment or is sharply moderated by graph context.

Molecule-novel para-bromoacetophenone m30 at 10/1 pairs with the selected ortho isomer m43 under the same ratio and loading-solvent conditions. Recorded densities and resulting masses differ slightly, so this is a conditional positional-substitution comparison rather than a perfectly isolated structural effect.

m43 at 10/1, 100 uL extends its compact measured 2/1 anchor 8abfe1426e39da061663 and supplies the reference for the selected para-bromo isomer. These ordinary aromatic-ketone labels help determine whether corrections from polar carbonyl failures should transfer to this common compact region.

Molecule-novel fluoropropiophenone m65 at 5/1 tests transfer from the pyridyl propiophenone failure 49201b5817f204116f7f. The shared acyl framework but different ring heteroatom environment makes its low predicted retention informative for learning when the basic-ring correction should apply.

Molecule-novel diphenylmethane m214 at 50/1 provides a two-ring hydrocarbon reference beside the ether and amine families. Measured 27c21665105a4679a090 and 70cba7a21b5a01fb8e73 show very different retention in related linker contexts; this label helps bound transfer to a graph with no heteroatom binding site.

m45 at 50/1, 100 uL extends the bromocarboxylic acid beyond measured 5/1 record 5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6 and 10/1 record d43d692e19100ebe5646. It tests acid-specific endpoint growth and whether the broad acid behavior represented by m173 transfers to a smaller aliphatic acid.

m197 at 50/1, 100 uL tests whether salicylaldehyde's broad finishes at 1/1 and 5/1 in 739f955977aa740524e5 and d227db4f4b8fdca822d5 grow further in weaker eluent. Comparison with brominated and methoxy analogs can teach structural control of onset and finish without assuming intramolecular hydrogen bonding determines the result.

m205 at 5/1, 150 uL completes the loading series containing 7954bf73f74c7fbcecb2 and 48853fd78c77153b963a. The existing pair has earlier onset but later finish at higher loading; the third point tests whether that endpoint asymmetry continues and constrains a historically severe failure region.

m135 at 5/1, 150 uL bridges measured 2/1 record 82b6eb1475767aca619f and the late 10/1 response in 75232f4ee5de52a0499e. Pairing it with the methoxybenzyl-alcohol experiment tests how aromatic substitution changes the transition, while accounting for their different recorded loading masses.

m120 at 5/1, 150 uL adds an intermediate response for methoxybenzyl alcohol beyond measured 1/1 record 2bd6619109218dcf6580. Together with m135 and the measured methoxyphenylethanol record e6e78489d1da4066c07e, it tests substitution and hydroxyl-linker context in the alcohol family.

m4 at 50/1, 100 uL tests a high-CW-distance prediction of substantially later elution for a fused aromatic graph without polar heteroatoms. Measured low-ratio anchor a539b04b0ab3606e7dd3 does not establish this high-ratio rise. The label can distinguish genuine aromatic retention from broad-response transfer learned from polar scaffolds.

Molecule-novel methyl chlorobenzoate m102 at 20/1 tests ester-alkyl transfer from ethyl chlorobenzoate observations 89b6013d19ba95312c59 and c16aef24cbedd5b1b875. It adds a common neutral ester graph at an informative intermediate ratio and helps bound broad-tail corrections outside donor-rich chemistry.

Molecule-novel methyl bromoisobutyrate m93 at 10/1 supplies a compact predicted ester anchor with substantial structural novelty. Measured related bromoesters d3f006ad008c95f61f09, 41ae24734eabf9cae4d7, and 6691aaf598ee5504e24b provide references for learning the joint effects of ester alkyl group, alpha branching, ratio, and loading.

hypotheses.content: Increasing the recorded PE/EA ratio weakens the normal-phase mobile phase and can produce nonlinear increases in V1 and V2. The location and endpoint shape of that increase are scaffold-specific.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate labels distinguish transition location from a molecule-wide retention offset and teach when onset and finish require different condition responses.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the matched intermediate points for m141, m31, m209, m72, and m199 reveal continued growth, a delayed transition, or a plateau?

hypotheses.content: Loading responses can be endpoint-asymmetric, scaffold-dependent, and sometimes nonmonotonic. Nearly invariant current predictions across loading levels may miss useful relationships, but measured contrasts do not establish a universal causal loading rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading labels can improve separate V1 and V2 responses and prevent transfer of one scaffold's loading direction to unrelated rows. Repeated-condition variability limits mechanistic conclusions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m19 interpolate smoothly between its onset-shifted endpoints, and do m90, m205, and m141 retain their observed onset-versus-finish asymmetry at the selected conditions?

hypotheses.content: Functional-group environment and graph topology influence retention and condition sensitivity beyond coarse polarity counts. Positional substitution, carbonyl conjugation, ring size, linker identity, and basic-site environment are plausible transferable distinctions, with their individual mechanisms still untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related-graph comparisons can teach where a correction should transfer and where it should stop. Compact neutral references are particularly useful alongside broad polar examples; differences in recorded loading conditions must remain part of the comparison.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which distinctions transfer across the new fused ketone, conjugated ketone, halogenated ketone, ester, and hydrocarbon graphs, and which require scaffold-specific condition responses?

hypotheses.content: The previous hypothesis that m202 generally maintains compact elution intervals across its response surface is weakened. Its conflicting 10/1 loading records require testing before compactness or broadening is generalized to other conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: At 10/1, the 50, 100, and 150 uL measurements are respectively 14.79/21.41, 35.08/70.35, and 4.62/9.38 mL. Both a reproducible ratio-by-loading interaction and unresolved row variability remain possible. Blanket compact or broad-tail corrections could therefore mislead retraining.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 5/1, does the 100 uL row again elute substantially later and more broadly than the 50 uL row, or does their contrast largely disappear?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes support moving from the now well-sampled m146 and m206 curves toward missing intermediate points and related graphs. Their measured low-to-high ratio responses are substantial, while many recent intermediate predictions were reasonably close. The historical V2 misses for m141 at 20/1 (about -47 mL) and m37 at 20/1 (about -32 mL) show that genuine broad finishes remain underlearned; accurate m119 at 2/1 and m199 at 5/1 argue against applying a blanket broadening correction. Loading evidence became more specific: m19 shifts onset by roughly 10 mL between 50 and 150 uL with almost unchanged finish; m146 and m205 show other endpoint asymmetries; m211 remains nonmonotonic across its three high-ratio loading levels. The latest m202 result was narrower than predicted, but the full observed table includes a much broader 100 uL measurement, so I weakened the earlier scaffold-wide compactness interpretation. The m195 150 uL record also has V1 slightly above V2, making record variability an explicit alternative to a smooth loading explanation. I corrected two trajectory interpretation errors: higher PE/EA means weaker mobile phase, and PE/DCM entries here identify loading solvents. Also, fe7e8ceb4ace767f1df2 is observed m143 at 2/1, not m209 at 10/1; m209 therefore still needs that intermediate measurement. Historical acquisition errors were used as feedback, not treated as current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines failure repair with experiments that can define transferable relationships. Matched ratio points for m141, m31, m209, m36, m72, and m199 locate transitions or test predicted plateaus. Loading contrasts for m19, m90, m205, and m202 address specific observed endpoint patterns that the current predictor often represents almost identically across mass. The m195 point probes an inconsistent local surface without assuming its unusual record is a physical law. New m179 points distinguish scaffold offset from condition sensitivity, while related ketone, alcohol, ester, and hydrocarbon comparisons test the boundaries of graph transfer. Compact predicted controls and the nonpolar m4 challenge help protect common rows from corrections learned on broad polar intervals. The m72 loading-solvent pair changes both solvent identity and loading-solvent volume, so only their joint effect is identifiable. Quantile widths and CW distance informed the choices but were not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty; experimental interval width was treated as a target property. Together, these labels should improve conditional structure representations and both endpoints across the Row-distribution, rather than merely targeting the largest predicted volumes.
